name: Match Clock
description: Periods, stoppages, and overtime: the official time a match is played against, distinct from utility.timer_system's raw countdown. It owns period structure (halves, quarters), stoppage accounting — the clock pauses while the drama doesn't — and the overtime rule as a plug point, because golden goal versus shootout is a config row, not a code branch. Score-triggered resets listen to world.goalScored so kickoff timing survives ruleset changes without a rewire. It displays nothing: ui.hud renders utility.periodStarted and utility.periodEnded like any other timer event, and the clock never learns what a scoreboard looks like.

inputs.name: periodCount
inputs.description: Halves, quarters, or innings — same mechanism, different count. Two halves with a midpoint break is the default because the break is where substitutions and strategy talks live.

inputs.name: periodLengthSeconds
inputs.description: Regulation length of one period. Five minutes is the video-game half: long enough for a comeback narrative, short enough that a blowout ends before it curdles.

inputs.name: stoppageTime
inputs.description: Whether dead time is banked and replayed at period end. On by default because stoppage time is where the genre keeps its last-gasp goals; arcade modes turn it off and get a cleaner clock.

inputs.name: overtimeRule
inputs.description: What a tied regulation produces: 'golden_goal', 'extra_periods', or 'shootout'. The clock sequences whichever rule is named; the rule's resolution logic belongs to whoever owns its mechanics.

inputs.name: overtimeLengthSeconds
inputs.description: Length of an overtime period when the rule needs one. Ignored entirely under golden goal, which is the point of keeping it separate — the clock should not know why it is running.

outputs.name: currentPeriod
outputs.description: 1-indexed period in progress, or the regulation count plus one during overtime. Commentary, HUD, and stamina drain modifiers all read this one number.

outputs.name: clockSeconds
outputs.description: Official time remaining in the period, frozen during stoppages. This is the authoritative match clock; utility.timer_system underneath is just the metronome.

outputs.name: isOvertime
outputs.description: True once regulation ends tied. Rule systems gate on this rather than comparing scores themselves, because 'tied at the whistle' is a moment, not a query.
